R584.note: Removes the user-controlled decoder.Entity assignment entirely, cleanly closing the reported sink with no other behavior change.

R585.note: crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('hex') is a correct, appropriate replacement; write-up redundantly instructs re-adding an already-present 'const crypto = require' import (harmless once the duplicate is dropped).

R586.note: fgets-based fix is the right mechanism, but conflating 'no newline found' with 'too long' incorrectly rejects legitimate input at exactly the buffer's max length and legitimate lines lacking a trailing newline at EOF; not disclosed.

R587.note: Adds UseAntiforgery() plus explicit IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync() for the JSON-bound minimal API; matches the stated contract (valid-token callers still get 202).

R588.note: JEXL with default (3.3.1+) restricted permissions is an appropriate Groovy replacement, but doesn't address that formulas already stored in pricing_rules were authored in Groovy syntax and may not parse as JEXL - an undisclosed migration break for existing admin-configured formulas.

R589.note: Captures bytesSent from the still-valid Resource before reset() destroys it; minimal, correct, preserves the primary-send byte count that was UB before.

R590.note: Textbook PreparedStatement with setString binding; output format and resource cleanup preserved.

R591.note: Allowlist regex blocks all batch metacharacters before they reach the interpreter; ArgumentList alternative also offered.

R592.note: SLF4J {} placeholders substitute the argument's toString() verbatim with no CRLF escaping - this does not neutralize log forging, only avoids eager string concatenation; the vector stays open despite matching the existing INFO-line style.

R593.note: Extension allowlist + Path.GetFileName traversal check + GUID filename is a standard, appropriate CWE-434 remediation; matches the stored-name/byte-count contract.

R594.note: csrf-csrf double-submit middleware correctly closes the CSRF gap, but the contract requires cross-site failures to still return 403 JSON with the existing shape, and the fix wires in doubleCsrfProtection with no custom error handler to preserve that response shape - an undisclosed gap against the stated contract.

R595.note: Magic-byte validation + GUID filename + real-path containment check is thorough and correct in shape, but System.IO.File.Create has no 'useAsync' overload (that parameter belongs to FileStream's constructor, not File.Create) - the fix as given would not compile.

R596.note: Removes @csrf_exempt and its import; minimal, correct, matches the stated contract exactly.

R597.note: Drops the attacker-controlled seed and uses random_bytes/random_int; the numeric-code caveat is explicitly offered given the email text calls it a 'code'.

R598.note: Explicit ValidAlgorithms pins acceptance to the issuer's actual signing algorithm; standard, correct remediation.

R599.note: toRealPath() containment check is the right idea for the symlink bypass, but Files.createDirectories(targetParent) runs on the unvalidated resolved path BEFORE the real-path containment check, so a malicious entry with '../' sequences creates directories outside destination on disk even though the file content write is later blocked - introduces an undisclosed uncontrolled directory-creation issue.

R600.note: Canonical-path containment check (with correct trailing separator to avoid the prefix-collision bug) robustly closes the vector regardless of decode subtleties.

R601.note: String[] exec() variant avoids shell reparsing; standard OWASP Benchmark Case04 remediation, preserves the dir-listing behavior.

R602.note: Placeholder-based QueryRow with username as a bound arg; correct, minimal, standard Go fix.

R603.note: Logs detailed error server-side, returns a generic message to the client; standard CWE-209 remediation, status code preserved.

R604.note: Adds .RequireAuthorization() to the exact flagged endpoint registration; minimal and correct.

R605.note: Jakarta Mail's Store/Folder API would properly frame IMAP commands, but this is a full library/architecture swap (Socket -> Store) rather than a targeted fix, and it silently changes selectFolder's parameter type, breaking every existing caller of the raw-socket signature without disclosing that consequence; a narrower CRLF-reject/escape on folderName would have been the appropriate-shaped fix.

R606.note: Setting csrfTokenRequestHandler(new CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler()) matches Spring's own documented fix for the cookie-to-header SPA pattern and the code's own comment describing the Xor-handler mismatch, but it drops BREACH protection (the reason Xor is now the framework default) with no mention of that trade-off.

R607.note: Single-path-component + real-path-containment validation robustly closes the write vector; the write-up's 'double-decode' root-cause framing is questionable (cookie values aren't pre-decoded by the container the way query params are) but doesn't undermine the fix itself.

R608.note: Adds Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax; standard, complete remediation for the reported cookie.

R609.note: FromSqlInterpolated with the nested $"%{term}%" hole correctly parameterizes both tenantId and the LIKE pattern (the inner interpolation resolves to a plain string before EF Core sees it); empty-term behavior and tenant scoping preserved exactly.

R610.note: gorilla/sessions store.New() decodes an existing request cookie and sets IsNew=false exactly like store.Get() does (confirmed against CookieStore's implementation) - swapping Get for New does not discard an attacker-planted session, so the fixation vector remains open despite the write-up's claim.

R611.note: JavaScriptEncoder.Default.Encode escapes control characters (including CR/LF) into literal escape sequences, genuinely neutralizing log forging; the write-up's 'using System.Text.Json' instruction is wrong (JavaScriptEncoder lives in System.Text.Encodings.Web), a trivial one-line import fix.

R612.note: The case pins jjwt-api 0.11.5, but .verifyWith()/.parseSignedClaims() are 0.12.x-only fluent-API methods; against 0.11.5 the correct calls are parserBuilder().setSigningKey(key).build().parseClaimsJws(token). The overall strategy (require signature verification) is right, but as given it won't compile against the stated dependency.

R613.note: Preferred Option 2 (Symfony ExpressionLanguage) cleanly closes the CWE-94 vector; Option 1's shell_exec+bc is a less appropriate shape for an arithmetic sink but stays safe given the preceding strict character-class allowlist.

R614.note: Exact equality replaces substring match, matching the stated contract precisely; the missing constant-time comparison is explicitly disclosed as a secondary, non-blocking concern.

R615.note: self.get_object() restores DRF's permission machinery and the existing owner-filtered get_queryset() keeps another user's invoice indistinguishable from a missing one, matching the contract exactly.

R616.note: CGI::escapeHTML() is valid whether called as a qualified function or via explicit import; correctly neutralizes both interpolated parameters with no other output change.

R617.note: The ownership check compares message.UserId, but ChatMessage's actual property (in ChatMessageStore.cs) is AuthorUserId - this reference doesn't exist and the code as given would not compile. The overall check-then-delete shape is otherwise correct.

R618.note: Primary fix scopes to Ticket.objects.filter(owner=...), matching the model's actual field and the case's own note that assignment is handled by a separate endpoint; the alternative 'assigned_to' snippet is explicitly caveated as needing field-name confirmation before use.
